digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate and completion-verifier evidence contract
propositions: Gates cannot audit measurement provenance because plan-review runs before evidence exists and completion-verifier accepts operator attestation on trust by design; evidence grounding is structurally incomplete without recording measurement context as queryable text.

Live cloud measurements taken under broader privilege than production (e.g., bedrock:* identity) cannot fail and carry zero discriminatory information; policy simulators cannot distinguish between whether a named action is permitted versus which action a service actually checks, producing confident wrong conclusions.

Plans asserting unchanged behaviour across substrate/route/provider swaps while citing only configuration (not resolution paths) hide defects: the ground truth is in-repo and reachable, but invisible because uncited dependencies are not examined by reviewers.

Operator-attested evidence contract must deterministically capture measurement provenance (environment, principal, privilege posture, instrument type) to enable repo-grounded contradiction detection without re-running world measurements.

An epic-level plan-review can pass and sign while child stories remain unreviewed at claim time, leaving story-level defects unexamined; decompositions need mechanisms cited somewhere to guard against this visibility gap.
